nodes.label: Conjecture 1
nodes.content: Any compact Hermitian manifold with constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature must be either Kahler or Chern flat. A long-standing open question in non-Kahler geometry; known in dimension 2 and several special cases.

nodes.label: Theorem 1
nodes.content: Chen-Chen-Nie and Huang-Wan: let (M^n,g) be a compact locally conformally Kahler manifold with constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature. Then it must be Kahler, hence a complex space form. External cited result (CCN, HW) resolving Conjecture 1 in the lcK case; motivates and provides the technique borrowed for this paper.

nodes.label: Conjecture 2
nodes.content: Any compact Hermitian manifold with constant Levi-Civita holomorphic sectional curvature must be either Kahler or Levi-Civita flat. The Levi-Civita analogue of Conjecture 1; established in dimension 2. Confirmed for compact lcK manifolds by Theorem 2 (thm1).

nodes.label: Conjecture 3
nodes.content: Any compact Hermitian manifold with non-zero constant Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature must be Kahler (non-zero required, since there are examples with vanishing Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature that are not Bismut flat). The Bismut analogue; established in dimension 2. Confirmed for compact lcK manifolds by Theorem 3 (thm2).

nodes.label: Theorem 2
nodes.content: Main result (Levi-Civita case): let (M^n,g) be a compact locally conformally Kahler manifold. If its Levi-Civita holomorphic sectional curvature is constant, then it must be Kahler, hence a complex space form. Proof: globally conformally Kahler case via Proposition 2 (prop2); strict lcK case via Proposition 1 (prop1) and the Kamishima-Fried uniformization Theorem 6 (thm:uniformization), ruling out non-exact Lee form by a pluriharmonic/maximum-principle argument.

nodes.label: Theorem 3
nodes.content: Main result (Bismut case): let (M^n,g) be a compact locally conformally Kahler manifold. If its Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature is a constant c, then either g is Kahler (a complex space form), or c=0 and (M^n,g) is an isosceles Hopf manifold. Proof mirrors Theorem 2: globally conformally Kahler case via Proposition 2 (prop2); strict case via Proposition 1 (prop1) and Theorem 6 (thm:uniformization), analyzing the deck-transformation action on a pluriharmonic function.

nodes.label: Lemma 1
nodes.content: For a metric connection D on a Hermitian manifold (M^n,g): H^D is identically c iff the symmetrized curvature hat R^D_{i bar j k bar l} = (c/2)(g_{i bar j} g_{k bar l} + g_{i bar l} g_{k bar j}) under any local (1,0) frame. States constant holomorphic sectional curvature as a symmetrized-curvature identity. (Well-known; proof omitted.)

nodes.label: Lemma 2
nodes.content: Under a local unitary frame, the Bismut and Levi-Civita curvatures are related to the Chern curvature by explicit formulas (eq:RbR) and (eq:RgR) involving Chern torsion components T^j_{ik} and their covariant derivatives. Proof by matrix computation of connection/curvature forms (following YangZ).

nodes.label: Corollary 4
nodes.content: Under any local unitary frame, symmetrizing (eq:RbR) and (eq:RgR) and using skew-symmetry of torsion gives hat{R^b} = hat R - Q and hat{R^g} = hat R - (1/2)Q, with Q an explicit quadratic expression in the Chern torsion. Follows from Lemma 2 by symmetrization.

nodes.label: Lemma 3
nodes.content: Huang-Wan: for a Hermitian manifold (M^n,g), if P is a Hermitian symmetric (1,1) tensor with L_g(P)=0 then P=0; i.e. the map L_g is injective. External cited result (HW, Lemma 3.1); proof reproduced. Used to pass parallelism of curvature to parallelism of the potential tensor.

nodes.label: Lemma 4
nodes.content: A Kahler manifold (M^n,g) is Bochner-Kahler iff there exists a Hermitian symmetric (1,1) tensor P with R = L_g(P). Provides the algebraic criterion for Bochner-Kahlerness used to identify Bochner-Kahler metrics arising from constant holomorphic sectional curvature.

nodes.label: Theorem 5
nodes.content: Kamishima / Bryant: let (M^n,g) be a complete Bochner-Kahler manifold. Then its universal cover is holomorphically isometric to M^p_kappa x M^{n-p}_{-kappa} for some kappa and 1 <= p <= n; in particular g is locally symmetric. External cited result. Used in the globally conformally Kahler case to conclude local symmetry.

nodes.label: Lemma 5
nodes.content: Under a unitary frame e for g and the corresponding frame for the conformal metric h = e^{2u} g, the Chern curvature and torsion components transform by the explicit conformal-change formulas (eq:RhR) and (eq:ThT). (Standard computation; see YangZ.)

nodes.label: Proposition 1
nodes.content: Let (M^n,g) be Hermitian and h = e^{2u} g with u real smooth. If h is Kahler and g has constant Chern (or Levi-Civita, or Bismut) holomorphic sectional curvature, then h is Bochner-Kahler. Proof: in each case, symmetrizing the conformal curvature relation writes R^h = L_h(A) for an explicit (1,1) tensor A, using Lemma 1 (H = c as symmetrized identity) and, in the Bismut/Levi-Civita cases, Corollary 4 (the Q correction); Lemma 4 then gives Bochner-Kahlerness.

nodes.label: Proposition 2
nodes.content: Let (M^n,g) be compact Hermitian with h = e^{2u} g Kahler for some smooth real u. If g has constant Chern, Bismut, or Levi-Civita holomorphic sectional curvature, then g is Kahler, hence a complex space form. Proof: Proposition 1 gives h Bochner-Kahler, then Theorem 5 gives h locally symmetric, so R^h = L_h(A) is parallel; injectivity of L_h (Lemma 3) makes A parallel; an eigenvalue/maximum-principle analysis forces g Kahler.

nodes.label: Theorem 6
nodes.content: Kamishima-Fried uniformization (via Huang-Wan): let (M^n,g) be a compact lcK manifold, n >= 2, with non-exact Lee form, whose associated Kahler metric tilde h is Bochner-Kahler. Then up to scaling, (tilde M, tilde h) is holomorphically isometric to (C^n minus {0}, h_0) with Euclidean h_0, and every deck transformation has the form gamma(z) = r_gamma U_gamma z with r_gamma > 0, U_gamma in U(n), and r_gamma != 1 for at least one gamma. External cited result (HW, Prop 5.1). Crucial tool in the strict lcK case of Theorems 2 and 3.
